trace.title: Repository query
trace.detail:
# The idea

JPA maps objects to relational rows. Hibernate is a common implementation.

A repository is an access boundary; it does not remove the need to reason about SQL.

An entity loaded inside a persistence context is managed. Changing it can produce an UPDATE when work is flushed.

Flush sends SQL; commit makes the transaction durable. They are not the same event.

A detached object is no longer tracked by that context.

Associations can hide database work. Reading 20 tasks and then each task.owner.name can issue 21 queries.

That is N+1: one list query plus one per item. Choose a fetch plan or a DTO query for this screen.

Do not switch every relation to eager loading; that can load a huge graph.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Ask what SQL runs at each line. The repository list call loads task rows.

A lazy owner access can trigger another query while the context is open. Outside it, an uninitialized association may fail.

Build the response inside a deliberate read boundary. Count queries with test instrumentation or SQL logs in a sandbox.

Compare one item and twenty items. A constant small query count is evidence; the word repository is not.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail:
An in-memory H2 test may hide PostgreSQL behavior. SQL logs can also expose values, so use synthetic test data.

A uniqueness pre-check without a database constraint can race.
